blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
End-to-end supply chain visibility, at executive level, is less a dashboard and more a discipline. It is the ability to answer, at any moment, three questions honestly: where is every important shipment right now, what is likely to happen to each of them over the next two weeks, and which of those likely events would actually matter to the business if they went wrong.

Very few companies have this. Most have partial visibility — one leg of the journey is tracked, and the rest is filled in with hope and phone calls. The gap matters, because the earlier a problem is seen, the more options are available and the less expensive the fix is.

Building real visibility requires investment in data feeds, agreements with partners who may not naturally share, and a cultural willingness to look at bad news early rather than explain it away later. The companies that invest this way acquire, over time, a competitive advantage that is quiet, permanent, and almost impossible to copy from the outside.

items.q: How does the text define executive-level visibility?
options: As a discipline rather than a dashboard
items.why: "less a dashboard and more a discipline" — o texto contrasta ferramenta com prática.

items.q: What is described as "partial visibility"?
options: One leg tracked and the rest filled in with hope and phone calls
Visibility limited to the origin only
items.why: "one leg of the journey is tracked, and the rest is filled in with hope and phone calls."

items.q: According to the text, why does seeing a problem earlier matter?
options: It removes the need for data feeds
It guarantees the shipment arrives on time
More options are available and the fix is less expensive
It reduces the number of partners involved
items.why: "the earlier a problem is seen, the more options are available and the less expensive the fix is."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The advantage from real visibility is hard to copy
Partial visibility leaves a costly gap
Buying a dashboard is enough to achieve end-to-end visibility
Real visibility depends on a cultural willingness to face bad news early
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que visibilidade é disciplina, não painel — comprar um dashboard, sozinho, não basta.

items.q: The phrase "quiet, permanent, and almost impossible to copy" suggests that the advantage…
options: is built slowly and cannot be bought off the shelf by rivals
will fade once competitors notice it
items.why: Inferência: "acquire, over time" e "impossible to copy from the outside" indicam vantagem construída, não adquirida rapidamente.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o caso de investimento à diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. I know none of us enjoyed the last two weeks, so let me be direct about what actually happened. A shipment was delayed at a transhipment hub, the delay was known locally for eleven days, and it was not seen by anyone here until the customer called. That is not a data problem. It is a visibility problem, and it cost us far more than the shipment itself.

What I am asking the board to approve is not a dashboard. Dashboards are the easy part. What I am asking for is investment in the data feeds and, harder still, in the agreements with partners who are not naturally inclined to share their numbers with us.

Some of you will ask whether the return justifies the spend. My honest answer is that most of the value is defensive. It will rarely be celebrated, because a disruption that is caught early and quietly fixed never becomes a story. But it is precisely those non-stories that protect the margin.

If this is approved today, the first origins are connected within the quarter. If it is not, I would simply ask that we agree, on the record, to stop being surprised.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Emily, how long was the delay known locally before anyone at the board saw it?
items.why: "the delay was known locally for eleven days."

items.q: What is Emily specifically asking the board to approve?
options: Investment in data feeds and data-sharing agreements with partners
A replacement for the transhipment hub
items.why: "investment in the data feeds and… the agreements with partners who are not naturally inclined to share."

items.q: How does Emily describe most of the value of the investment?
items.why: "most of the value is defensive… It will rarely be celebrated."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says the value comes from "non-stories"?
options: Problems solved quietly before they escalate leave no dramatic story
The board should not share results publicly
Nobody will write about the company
The data is not worth reporting
items.why: Inferência: uma disrupção pega cedo e resolvida em silêncio nunca vira caso — é aí que a margem é protegida.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's closing tone?
options: Pointed — offering a clear choice with mild pressure
items.why: Inferência: ela propõe uma decisão concreta e, se recusada, pede que a diretoria assuma o risco 'on the record'.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We only track one leg of the journey; the ocean crossing is a blind spot." A leg is…
options: a single stage or segment of a route
items.why: Leg = trecho: um segmento específico do percurso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Real-time tracking depends on a reliable ___ from each carrier's system."
items.why: Data feed = fluxo de dados, a fonte que alimenta o rastreamento.

items.q: "The team kept trying to explain away the delay instead of acting on it." To explain away means to…
options: dismiss or rationalise so it seems unimportant
items.why: Explain away = racionalizar, minimizar um problema até parecer irrelevante.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Sharing sensitive numbers with a partner requires a genuine ___, not just a signed contract."
items.why: Cultural willingness = disposição cultural para compartilhar, além do que o contrato exige.

items.q: "Our visibility is still partial, so we react late." Partial here means…
options: incomplete — covering only part of the chain
items.why: Partial = parcial: cobre só parte do percurso, deixando lacunas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre supply chain. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the visibility budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the tracking to the Brazilian origins first." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, região por região.

items.q: "Two carriers pushed back on sharing their raw data." They…
options: resisted or objected to the request
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente recusar de vez.

items.q: "They approved the pilot but never followed through on the full rollout." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "A prettier dashboard alone will not move the needle on response time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.
